admission.justification: The recorded behavioral fixture assertions guard this obligation; the proof facets distinguish their limited fixture behavior from real-host or full-final acceptance.

applicability: The native candidate-receipt walks and yielded-path/read/drain budget of one delivery sweep.
conditions: A sweep yields at most thirty-two candidate paths and reads at most thirty-two receipts.
Each directory listing may materialize and sort that directory once per pass for stable rotation, as the owner disposition permits.
The sweep skips history and message-binding subtrees before descending.
exclusions: A constant bound on all names in one directory or on execution-root discovery.
An elapsed-time ceiling; this implementation states path/read/drain ceilings.
Zero rglob yields as a proof that every enumeration API yielded zero names.

evidence: mcp/tests/test_held_queue.py::HeldSweepBoundsTests::test_idle_fleet_reads_stay_bounded_at_two_sizes passes with zero rglob yields; scratch/worker/5e0b3a10-7a35-4c5e-9f11-100000000001/xdg/r6-probe-after.txt sha 628ed08eb73c: 0 enumerated paths all six cycles at 64/256, reads<=32 (rglob API; per-directory scandir listings materialize once per pass, disclosed residual for Architect inspection)

statement: Each sweep tick pulls at most 32 candidate paths from resumable per-root walks and reads at most 32 receipts; no recursive glob runs in the tick, history and bindings are never descended into, and walks restart each pass so every receipt is visited.
